summary: Describes the individuals and organizations involved in the IETF, including the IESG, the working groups, and the relationship with the Internet Society. It is a best current practice, and it was replaced by RFC 9281.

eli5.summary: This is a who's who of the groups that make internet rules. It tells you who does what.

what do the iesg and working groups do
what is the difference between the ietf and the iab
subtitle: A who's who of the people and bodies that produce Internet standards, as of 1996.

tldr.problem: Anyone following the Internet standards process needs to know which individuals and organizations take part in it and what each of them is responsible for.
tldr.mechanism: The memo lists the key individuals (RFC Editor, Working Group chair, document editor) and the key organizations (IETF, its Working Groups, the Secretariat, the Internet Society, the IESG, the IAB, IANA and the IRTF) and describes each one's role.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2028 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 11) that has since been obsoleted by RFC 9281, so it describes the arrangement as of October 1996 rather than today.

facts.label: IESG composition
facts.value: Area Directors plus the IETF chair

today: RFC 2028 has been obsoleted by RFC 9281, so it describes the arrangement as of October 1996. It has also been updated by RFC 3668, RFC 3979 and RFC 8717.

sections.title: Scope of the Memo
sections.content:
RFC 2028 describes the individuals and organizations involved in the IETF. It does not define the standards process itself. That is left to RFC 2026, which defines the stages of standardization, the requirements for moving a document between stages and the types of documents used. RFC 2026 also covers intellectual property rights and copyright for the process.

The memo is a Best Current Practice, numbered BCP 11, and it asks for discussion and suggestions for improvements.
sections.eli5: This memo does not say how rules get made. It only says who the people and groups are. The rulebook is a different document.

sections.title: Key Individuals
sections.content:
Three roles are described. The RFC Editor manages the RFC publication series. The editor may in practice be one or more individuals, and is responsible for the mechanics of publication and for upholding the traditionally high technical and editorial standards of the series.

A Working Group chair (or co-chairs) heads each IETF Working Group. The chair directs the group's activities, presides over its meetings and makes sure the group meets its commitments in the standards process. The chair is the formal point of contact between the group and the IESG, through the Area Director of the area to which the group is assigned.

A document editor is designated by a Working Group to make sure a document accurately reflects the decisions the group has made. As a general practice, the chair and the document editor are different people, to help ensure that documents reflect the group's consensus and that all processes are followed.
sections.eli5: Every club has a leader who runs the meetings and a note-taker who writes down what the club decided. They are usually different kids, so the notes stay fair.

sections.title: The IETF and Its Working Groups
sections.content:
The IETF is described as an open international community of network designers, operators, vendors and researchers concerned with the evolution of the Internet architecture and the smooth operation of the Internet. It is the principal body engaged in developing new Internet Standard specifications.

The technical work is done in Working Groups. They are organized by topic into several Areas (for example routing, network management and security) under the coordination of Area Directors. Working Groups typically have a narrow focus and a lifetime bounded by completion of a specific task, and new ones are established by explicit charter.

Membership is defined solely by individual participation. Participants act as individual technical contributors, not as formal representatives of organizations. Anyone with the time and interest may take part, IETF meetings are held three times a year, and in most cases participation is possible by electronic mail alone. Participants who discuss a specific technology must disclose to the Working Group chairs any relevant current or pending intellectual property rights that they reasonably and personally know of.
sections.eli5: Anybody who is interested can join a club, and they join as themselves, not as a company's spokesperson. Each club has one job, and when the job is done the club ends.

sections.title: Oversight: Secretariat, ISOC, IESG and IAB
sections.content:
The IETF Secretariat, made up of the IETF Executive Director and staff, performs the administrative functions. The Executive Director is the formal point of contact for the standards process and maintains its formal public record.

The Internet Society (ISOC) is an international organization with individual and organizational members, managed by a Board of Trustees. Internet standardization is an organized activity of the ISOC, and the Board of Trustees is responsible for ratifying the procedures and rules of the process.

The IESG manages the IETF's technical activities for the ISOC. It is composed of the Area Directors and the IETF chair, who also chairs the IESG. It handles the initial approval of new Working Groups and the final approval of specifications as Internet Standards.

The IAB is chartered by the ISOC Trustees to oversee the architecture of the Internet and its protocols. It appoints the IETF chair, approves other IESG candidates, reviews and approves charters of new Working Groups, and serves as an appeal board for complaints of improper execution of the standards process.
sections.eli5: Above the clubs there is a school office that does the paperwork, a steering committee that approves new clubs, and a board that checks the rules are followed and listens to complaints.

sections.title: IANA, the IRTF and Who Picks Whom
sections.content:
The IANA assigns the values of protocol parameters that must be unique, such as version numbers, protocol numbers, port numbers and MIB numbers. It publishes the current tables in RFCs titled "Assigned Numbers", and the memo calls it the "top of the pyramid" for DNS and Internet address assignment.

The IRTF is not directly involved in the standards process. It investigates topics considered too uncertain, too advanced or insufficiently well understood for standardization. When one of its activities produces a stable enough specification, it is processed through the IETF.

The members of the IESG and IAB are both nominated by a nominations committee (the Nomcom). The IAB approves the IESG members, and the ISOC board approves the IAB members. The memo also notes that the IESG charter "does not yet exist" and that the IANA and RFC Editor charters were still work in progress.
sections.eli5: One helper keeps the official list of names and numbers so nobody picks the same one twice. Another group tries out wild ideas that are not ready for the rulebook yet.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo's security section is a single sentence: security is not addressed in this memo. It describes organizations and roles, not a protocol, so there is nothing further to analyze.
sections.eli5: This memo is a list of who does what, so there is nothing to lock or unlock.
